content: Hemidesmus indicus, commonly known as Indian Sarsaparilla, is a plant species native to South Asia. It is a slender, twining shrub that can sometimes grow prostrate or semi-erect. The plant contains laticifers, which are specialized cells that produce latex. Its roots are woody and emit a distinct aromatic fragrance. The stems are numerous, slender, cylindrical in shape, and exhibit thickened nodes. The leaves grow in opposite pairs, are short-petioled, and vary significantly in shape, ranging from elliptic-oblong to linear-lanceolate. The flowers of Hemidesmus indicus are greenish on the outside and purplish on the inside. They are clustered in sub-sessile axillary cymes. This plant is utilized both as a beverage ingredient and in traditional medicine. In Ayurvedic medicine, it is referred to as ananthamoola or Anantmula and is also known as False Sarsaparilla. Hemidesmus indicus is recognized for its therapeutic properties, functioning as a tonic, alterative, demulcent, diaphoretic, diuretic, and blood purifier. It is traditionally used to address a variety of conditions, including nutritional disorders, syphilis, chronic rheumatism, urinary diseases such as gravel, and various skin conditions. The plant is typically administered in the form of powder, infusion, or decoction, and is often prepared as a syrup. It is also a key ingredient in several medicinal formulations. In Ayurveda, Hemidesmus indicus is classified as one of the Rasayana plants, which are known for their rejuvenating and anabolic effects. It promotes bile secretion and aids in detoxifying the body. The plant is a potent diuretic, capable of increasing urine output by three to four times. When combined with Tinospora, its therapeutic effects are further amplified. It is particularly effective in alleviating inflammation of the urethra, reducing burning sensations during urination, and managing advanced stages (third or fourth) of syphilis. Hemidesmus indicus is sometimes mistaken for another Ayurvedic herb called white sariva. Its root serves as a substitute for Sarsaparilla, which is derived from the dried root of tropical Smilax species, such as Smilax aspera L. and Smilax ovalifolia Roxb., found in India. However, it is important to distinguish it from American Sarsaparilla (Smilax aristolochaefolia Mill) and Jamaican Sarsaparilla (Smilax ornata Hook f). Chemical analysis of the root has revealed the presence of coumarins, volatile oils (with p-methoxy salicylic aldehyde as the primary component), two sterols, and a pregnane glycoside. Hemidesmus indicus is widely distributed across India, from the upper Gangetic plain to Assam, as well as in parts of central, western, and southern India.
